Vaping Teenagers [6203]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Vaping Proposal

Vaping was hailed as a way to quit smoking, instead it’s become a craze amongst young people, and has millions of teenagers hooked.

With flavours like bubblegum, toffee crunch and berry blasé, no wonder it appeals to teenagers. It was designed and marketed to them.

Kayla is 16 years old and goes to school in Somerset West. She says she is addicted to vaping. She has tried to give it up but she can’t. Feels that it is healthier than smoking.
Has tried smoking but doesn’t like the taste. Likes the fruity flavours that are available.
Kayla goes through withdrawal when she tries to give up. She has been smoking since she was 14. You know it’s bad but you don’t care. It’s an addiction. Has a hold of you.

Kayla has tried traditional cigarettes but likes the fruity tastes of vaping.

People who vape are 3 times more likely to become smokers according to a recent British Survey.

Kayla’s mother is a smoker. She knows her child vapes and doesn’t think she can stop it. She doesn’t allow her to smoke at home and will throw away her vapes if she finds them.

She is really concerned about the health aspects of her child smoking.

What we know at the moment is that vaping is not as harmful as smoking but no one know when inhaling a cocktail of liquids what long term exposure will be.

All of Kayla’s friends vape.

Andrew is a friend of Kayla’s and also vapes. They speak about vaping at school and the teachers not being able to pick it up because the smoke does not smell as pungent at traditional cigarettes. They buy juice for their vapes and also disposable ones. Neither Kayla or Andrew is too concerned about the consequences of vaping. They know it contains nicotine but won’t stop vaping.

How does it work. E cigarettes heat liquid that contains nicotine, high temperatures and creates a vapour which is inhaled.

The booming vaping market is not legislated in SA. The new Tobacco Products Control Act will be tightening the controls but it is still in draft phase at the moment.

Dr Sharon Nyatsanza from the National Council Against Smoking is very concerned about the future health of South African youth.

Addiction is usually established in young people, most smokers start smoking before the age of 18, and in South Africa this is as early as nine years old. What usually starts as experimentation largely leads to addiction and the risk of becoming a lifelong smoker. Neurobiologically, children are much more vulnerable than adults to nicotine addiction, and those who start using nicotine at a young age have greater nicotine dependence than those who start later.
Stopping tobacco and nicotine use in children before they start should therefore occupy a central part of any public health strategy. If child initiation is significantly reduced, the tobacco and nicotine business will not be sustainable, and it’s no secret that taxes contribute greatly to this objective.

One of the companies that made vaping cool in the US is Juul.
(One could buy them in SA through Takealot.)
Launched in 2015 device delivered 3 times more nicotine than their rivals.

Initially it was meant to be a device that stopped people smoking but their advertising campaign was targeted at the youth. A vibrant advert with young models using a stylish device. In South Africa Although there is no age that one is allowed to start smoking

Juul placed ads in teen magazines in the US. South Africa was no different in a study undertaken by Dr Catherine Egbe of the Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drug Research Unit of the Medical Research Council of South Africa in 2017, found the following.

“Another study showed strategic placement of e-cigarette vape shops as a form of promotion and advertisement in South Africa: Of the at least 240 vape shops identified in South Africa during 2020, 39% were within a 10 km radius of a university or college campus, and 65.3% were within a 20 km radius. Given the impact of advertising on youth and young adults, there is still need for regulation to remove e-cigarette advertising from youth-oriented media.”

Not only is vaping not regulated but it is not taxed. It is hoped that taxation will reduce the levels of addiction in the youth.

“In the face of competing interests from multiple groups, child interests must remain a key concern. Taxation is an important step, but other urgently required measures include regulation of child-friendly flavours, and restrictions on e-cigarette advertising, promotion and sponsorship. These are some of the measures included in the Control of Tobacco Products and Electronic Delivery Systems Bill, and will significantly contribute to reducing initiation, use among young people and addiction to e-cigarettes.”
Between 1993 and 2009, total taxes on cigarettes (including excise and sales taxes) in South Africa increased from 32% of retail price to 52%. During the same period, cigarette sales declined 30%, government revenue from tobacco taxes increased 800%, and smoking prevalence among adults decreased 25%.

Vaping Teenagers Script 12

Studio Intro
The sudden rise of e-cigarette use, or vaping, among youth has led to widespread concern among parents and the health industry.
Vaping is big business in SA, product sales pre-lockdown amounted to R1.25 billion.

Script

Mac
Are you addicted to vaping?

Marcus
To be honest, yes.

Mac
Do you know what the health impacts of this?

Marcus
It destroys your lungs, and makes your breathing worse. It makes it so you're going to die at a much earlier age.

Mac
So why are you doing it? You are giving me all the reasons not to do it?

Marcus
To be honest, if I could just stop tomorrow, then I would, but as I said, I am addicted.


V/O
Marcus is 14 years old.

Ghost inhale, dragon and waterfall are the names of e-cigarette smoke tricks.
These smoke wizards are followed by millions on social media. Impressive… but the reality is that most vapes - or e-cigarettes - contain one of the most addictive substances around - nicotine. It’s as hard to quit as heroin.

Friends Emilio, Sean and Marcus are in High School and have all tried vaping.

Sean
It just looks cool. I don’t know how to explain it.

Mac
What is so cool about it blowing the smoke?

Sean
The smoke and the tricks.

V/O
Vaping among teenagers has skyrocketed worldwide. There may be as many as 5 million children vaping in America alone, are South African teens following suit?

Mac
How popular would you say this is amongst, you know, your age group?


Sean
Very, very, very popular. Almost everybody we meet is doing it.

Link Mac
It’s not hard to see why these devices would appeal to teenagers. It’s the latest tech toy, it has a sleek design, and they’re easy to conceal; teenagers love the flavours and the buzz they get from them.

V/O
Seen as a safer way of lighting up – and less offensive to non-smokers - vapes are electronic devices that heat a nicotine liquid, which creates a vapour, that is inhaled. They can vary in shape, size and colour and come in thousands of flavours.

V/O
Ashleigh was 16 when she started vaping.

Ashleigh
I do it because it's a nice flavour and I don't always have sweets at home to have that sugary flavour from. So maybe it's just that it's convenient for that kind of sweetness.

V/O
With flavours like marshmallow milk, death by chocolate, fruit ice and gummy bear, the vaping industry has been criticised for marketing to teenagers.

NOW: Juul Labs is an E-cigarette maker in the United States, fined almost R 7.5 billion to settle claims that their aggressive marketing caused a surge in teen vaping.
Juul bought online ads on websites, including Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network to promote their product.

The American Food and Drug administration fined vape manufacturer JUUL LABS R7,5 billion for their aggressive marketing on children’s television networks. In a statement Juul said that the settlement is part of its commitment to resolve its past issues and combat underage use.

V/O
Ian Gourley - a marketing and design specialist - says social media helps to sell the forbidden fruit.

Mac
So interesting that e-cigarette companies are directly targeting these.

Ian
And the trick actually is, is that they don't need to target youth to directly and you scream out from the rooftops, the youth are not allowed to touch this product. Youth are not allowed to engage in this product and youth are not allowed to purchase this product. You tell that to anybody under the age of 18, and that's almost like a red rag to a bull.

Emilio
For me, it is all about the sweetness; if the sweetness is nice and it gives you a good head rush, that’s a flavour I would continue using.

Mac
So you guys like the head rush.

Boys
Yes

V/O
Richard van Zyl-Smit, a professor of Respiratory Medicine at UCT, looked at the vaping trends of 5500 students at upmarket high schools. The results are shocking.

Mac
Prof the last stats that were done around smokers and smoking was done in 2012. What does your study show?

Richard
The previous data for vaping is about 2% in men under the age of 19 and 2.9% I think, in women. We're looking in the region, of 15 to 20% of high schoolers. Some of our schools, we're seeing over 30% of matric students vaping, which is incredibly high.

V/O
That’s almost 1000% increase in 10 years. The study showed that 3 out of 10 pupils used their vapes within an hour of waking up, and almost a quarter couldn’t get through the day without vaping.

Richard
I mean, that's crazy high. It really is of serious concern to us.

V/O
When nicotine is inhaled, it takes just ten seconds for it to reach the brain. It releases dopamine which is a chemical that helps to relieve stress and improve mood. But long term, this toxic, addictive substance poses serious health risks, to the lungs, heart and brain.

https://www.drugwatch.com/e-cigarettes/nicotine/
https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/ershdb/emergencyresponsecard_29750028.html

Mac
Do you know what sort of the health implications of vaping are?

Ashleigh
It's not ideal, the health implications, but it is my choice. So I'll deal with what happens and comes with a health issue later on.


V/O
There was a time when smoking tobacco cigarettes was cool too, but with over 8 million related deaths a year, that reputation has been stubbed out.
The impact of smoking on health is well documented; there are over 7000 toxic chemicals in a burning cigarette, some known to cause cancer.

(Pause)
Studies have shown that vaping is less harmful than smoking, but Prof van Zyl-Smit says not for adolescents, whose brains are still developing.




Richard
Adolescents learn fast, they laying down pathways. Nicotine is a psychoactive drug. It works in the brain and it interferes with those laying down of pathways.

So there are concerns about cognitive function, ability to function at school, memory, even school performance. And then more concerning long term effects about depression, anxiety disorders going on to other drugs.

Emilio
Yes. Why? It's, it's like first thing in the morning you wake up, take a few months of your vape and you just your whole body just feels heavy. Your nervous system is like.

Nice. It's nice if you call me.

Emilio
Down it just like it just brings you to, like, a whole.

Link
Vaping is believed to be less harmful than combustible cigarettes but there are no long term health impacts done on e-cigarettes.

Richard
The chemicals in e-cigarettes are far fewer than the chemicals in tobacco. Everyone would agree with that, but they still exist. So they still cancer-causing drugs in e-cigarettes. There's still toxins, and there's still pollutants, but at much lower levels.

V/O
Parents like Debbie, who has a teenager that has tried vaping, are understandably afraid.
Research shows that teens who use e-cigarettes are 4 times more likely to start smoking. Both Debbie’s parents died from smoking related diseases and it’s a future she doesn’t wish on her son, Sean.

https://www.safetyandhealthmagazine.com/articles/20779-teens-who-vape-much-more-likely-to-move-on-to-smoking-study-finds

Debbie
It would affect his ability to think in the classroom. It's a no no. He shouldn't have a vape and he knows that.
We don't know the long term effects of these vapes and what they're going to be doing, and nobody seems to care.

V/O
Dr Sharon Nyatsanza, from the National Council Against Smoking, does care and says legislation is needed to protect minors.

Mac
So am I correct in saying that for the past ten years, over a decade, e-cigarettes have been unregulated in South Africa?

Sharon
Yes, you're definitely correct. With e-cigarettes, they came in as consumer products. If they actually had registered as smoking cessation aids, like nicotine replacement therapies, then the medical council would have actually regulated them. That's why you see that no one knows. For example, the ingredients in the products. No-one knows the amount of nicotine.

V/O
The University of Kwa-Zulu Natal’s Pharmaceutical Sciences laboratory tested the nicotine levels of 12 e-juice samples for us.
Most were in spec or less, bar one that had 12mg more.
It’s not just nicotine, none of the other chemicals in e-juice have been proven to be safe when heated and inhaled.

Richard
So there is still cancer causing drugs in e-cigarettes , there is still toxins, there are still pollutants. But at much lower levels.



V/O
Parliament currently has legislation on the table to regulate the vaping industry.
In the 1990s, taxing cigarettes decreased smoking by 25 per cent.
The new bill is intended to have similar effects on the vaping industry.

Link
Not all of the shops enforce the strict no under 18 rule. Vapes are easily accessible; you can find them in petrol stations, supermarkets and even online.

Barry
If you come into our stores and we believe that you're not 18, we will ask you for your I.D. If we check the ID and we feel that it's fake, then we will confiscate the ID, and we have plenty of IDs This is not under 18.

V/O
E-Cigarettes were designed to help people stop smoking.
Smokers like Barry Buchman, who founded one of the largest vaping chains in South Africa.
(Pronounce “boeg”, as in branch of tree.)

Barry
Our target customer is someone who currently smokes who wants to stop smoking. We are absolutely against selling to people who have never smoked or vaped.

Mac
So what would you say? That there is a place for e-cigarettes?

Richard
Yeah, absolutely. I don't think anyone's calling for a ban on e-cigarettes. But there's absolutely no reason why they should be easily accessible to adolescents, marketed to adolescents.

V/O
The new bill should make it much harder for the youth to access e-cigarettes. But the teenagers we spoke to said that even with the nicotine tax, it wouldn’t stop their friends vaping.

Sean
They are so addictive that they can’t stop, they would smoke water, there is physically nothing you can do to make them stop and that’s the sad thing.

Marcus
If I could just stop tomorrow then I would but like I said I am addicted.

Mac
You think you are hooked now?

Marcus

Ya, a little bit.




PROMOS 1

Mac Link

A smoking teen every parent’s worst nightmare, but now adays they’re vaping is that because of the cool kid syndrome or is it sneaky advertising?









Promo 1 x 11 seconds

V/O

Vapes were designed to help people quit smoking.
Instead they’ve become millions of teenagers latest tech toy.

Sean
They just look cool.

Mac
What is cool, blowing the smoke?

Sean
The smoke and the tricks and the tricks.


Promo 2
New legislation is set to ban the promotion of e-cigarettes
Or is it already too late?

Up Sound
I am addicted.

Promo 3
Vaping is big business
But has the intended target shifted from cigarette addicts to teens?
But there's absolutely no reason why they should be easily accessible to adolescents, marketed to adolescents.

Almost a quarter of our school-going teens can’t get through a day without vaping.
How dangerous is the new cool?

Link Mac It’s not hard to see why these devices would appeal to teenagers. Emilio For me, it is all about the sweetness; if the sweetness is nice and it gives you a good head rush, that’s a flavour I would continue using. Mac So you guys like the head rush. Boys Yes V/O Richard van Zyl-Smit, a professor of Respiratory Medicine at UCT, looked at the vaping trends of 5500 students at upmarket high schools. The results are shocking. Mac Prof the last stats that were done around smokers and smoking was done in 2012. What does your study show? Richard The previous data for vaping is about 2% in men under the age of 19 and 2.9% I think, in women. We're looking in the region, of 15 to 20% of high schoolers. Some of our schools, we're seeing over 30% of matric students vaping, which is incredibly high. V/O That’s almost 1000% increase in 10 years. It releases dopamine which is a chemical that helps to relieve stress and improve mood. Ashleigh It's not ideal, the health implications, but it is my choice. So I'll deal with what happens and comes with a health issue later on. Richard Adolescents learn fast, they laying down pathways. Nicotine is a psychoactive drug. It works in the brain and it interferes with those laying down of pathways. metadata.Further information: Vaping Proposal Vaping was hailed as a way to quit smoking, instead it’s become a craze amongst young people, and has millions of teenagers hooked. With flavours like bubblegum, toffee crunch and berry blasé, no wonder it appeals to teenagers. It was designed and marketed to them. Kayla is 16 years old and goes to school in Somerset West. She says she is addicted to vaping. She has tried to give it up but she can’t. Feels that it is healthier than smoking. Has tried smoking but doesn’t like the taste. Likes the fruity flavours that are available. Kayla goes through withdrawal when she tries to give up. She has been smoking since she was 14. You know it’s bad but you don’t care. It’s an addiction. Has a hold of you. Kayla has tried traditional cigarettes but likes the fruity tastes of vaping. People who vape are 3 times more likely to become smokers according to a recent British Survey. Kayla’s mother is a smoker. She knows her child vapes and doesn’t think she can stop it. She doesn’t allow her to smoke at home and will throw away her vapes if she finds them. She is really concerned about the health aspects of her child smoking. What we know at the moment is that vaping is not as harmful as smoking but no one know when inhaling a cocktail of liquids what long term exposure will be. All of Kayla’s friends vape. Andrew is a friend of Kayla’s and also vapes. They speak about vaping at school and the teachers not being able to pick it up because the smoke does not smell as pungent at traditional cigarettes. They buy juice for their vapes and also disposable ones. Neither Kayla or Andrew is too concerned about the consequences of vaping. They know it contains nicotine but won’t stop vaping. How does it work. E cigarettes heat liquid that contains nicotine, high temperatures and creates a vapour which is inhaled. The booming vaping market is not legislated in SA. The new Tobacco Products Control Act will be tightening the controls but it is still in draft phase at the moment. Dr Sharon Nyatsanza from the National Council Against Smoking is very concerned about the future health of South African youth. Addiction is usually established in young people, most smokers start smoking before the age of 18, and in South Africa this is as early as nine years old. What usually starts as experimentation largely leads to addiction and the risk of becoming a lifelong smoker. Neurobiologically, children are much more vulnerable than adults to nicotine addiction, and those who start using nicotine at a young age have greater nicotine dependence than those who start later. Stopping tobacco and nicotine use in children before they start should therefore occupy a central part of any public health strategy. If child initiation is significantly reduced, the tobacco and nicotine business will not be sustainable, and it’s no secret that taxes contribute greatly to this objective. One of the companies that made vaping cool in the US is Juul. (One could buy them in SA through Takealot.) Launched in 2015 device delivered 3 times more nicotine than their rivals. Initially it was meant to be a device that stopped people smoking but their advertising campaign was targeted at the youth. A vibrant advert with young models using a stylish device. In South Africa Although there is no age that one is allowed to start smoking Juul placed ads in teen magazines in the US. South Africa was no different in a study undertaken by Dr Catherine Egbe of the Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drug Research Unit of the Medical Research Council of South Africa in 2017, found the following. “Another study showed strategic placement of e-cigarette vape shops as a form of promotion and advertisement in South Africa: Of the at least 240 vape shops identified in South Africa during 2020, 39% were within a 10 km radius of a university or college campus, and 65.3% were within a 20 km radius. Given the impact of advertising on youth and young adults, there is still need for regulation to remove e-cigarette advertising from youth-oriented media.” Not only is vaping not regulated but it is not taxed. It is hoped that taxation will reduce the levels of addiction in the youth. “In the face of competing interests from multiple groups, child interests must remain a key concern. Taxation is an important step, but other urgently required measures include regulation of child-friendly flavours, and restrictions on e-cigarette advertising, promotion and sponsorship. These are some of the measures included in the Control of Tobacco Products and Electronic Delivery Systems Bill, and will significantly contribute to reducing initiation, use among young people and addiction to e-cigarettes.” Between 1993 and 2009, total taxes on cigarettes (including excise and sales taxes) in South Africa increased from 32% of retail price to 52%. During the same period, cigarette sales declined 30%, government revenue from tobacco taxes increased 800%, and smoking prevalence among adults decreased 25%.
